method: Read R/label-utils.R, R/recode-with-table.R, R/merge-data.R, R/clean-variables.R, R/strings.R, DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, tests; fetched GitHub issue #159; ran three live Rscript repros against the working tree (devtools::load_all) at /tmp/v4-research/labels-repro{,2,3}.R; compared against recodeflow PR43 labels scoping documents.
summary: The labels layer is the part of cchsflow furthest from its own v4 scoping targets. Labels are built from per-row source-variable label columns in variable_details (variables.csv's label/labelLong columns are demonstrably dead), attached as sjlabelled-flavoured and ad-hoc attributes (factor + character-coded 'labels', plus custom 'labels_long'/'label_long'/'unit') that the labelled/haven ecosystem cannot consume, and fused to the recode engine with hidden type coercion and no opt-out. Live repros confirmed: (1) issue #159 is misdiagnosed - rec_with_table fails on ANY tibble input (including plain numeric tibbles) inside label_data's single-bracket indexing, while haven_labelled columns in a plain data.frame recode fine and haven::zap_labels does not fix it; (2) set_data_labels and merge_rec_data hard-stop on the package's own shipped metadata (DHHGAGE_cat5 has two distinct variableStartLabel values); (3) categorical missing is a literal factor level 'NA(b)' invisible to is.na(), inconsistent with the tagged_na encoding used for continuous variables, which both blocks haven::write_sav export and forces the new v3 clean layer to parse the legacy engine's own string output; (4) one catLabel mapping to multiple recEnd values silently drops value labels in 5 shipped variables; (5) labels do not survive bind_rows or base subsetting, so the canonical workflow is a full relabel via merge_rec_data, which hardcodes cchsflow:: worksheets. The fix direction is well-articulated in the labels scoping docs (haven_labelled output via the labelled package, separation of recode and label stages, sheets as single source of truth, labels on continuous special values) and matches CEP-017 v4 scope item 5 (decompose rec_with_table into detect/recode/derive/label stages).

issues.why_design_issue: The engine's only entry point silently assumes base-data.frame single-bracket semantics deep inside the label layer. Every modern import path (haven::read_sav, readr::read_csv, ODESSI PUMF distributions) returns tibbles, so the package fails on the data sources it exists to serve, and the open issue's proposed fix targets the wrong cause. A v4 that keeps column-extraction-by-`[ , ]` will re-inherit the bug.
issues.candidate_fix: Short term: replace `data_to_label[, variable_name]` with `data_to_label[[variable_name]]` throughout label_data (and audit recode-with-table.R for the same pattern), add a tibble + haven_labelled regression test, and correct the diagnosis on issue #159. v4: operate on extracted vectors and reassign once per column; accept any data.frame subclass.

The crash fires after all recoding work is done, in a utility whose job is cosmetic, and it fires on metadata the package itself ships. issues.why_design_issue: Missingness is the analytically load-bearing metadata in CCHS work, and the package encodes it two different ways depending on toType. The categorical encoding ('NA(b)' as a valid factor level) silently enters models, crosstabs and survey weights as a real category, and defeats every standard missing-data tool (is.na, na.omit, tidyr::drop_na). The dual encoding forces string round-tripping inside the package itself (clean-variables.R) and makes faithful export impossible. This is the single biggest semantic decision v4 must make.
issues.candidate_fix: Pick one ecosystem-native representation in v4: haven_labelled (numeric codes + tagged_na for missing, value labels on both valid and missing codes), with labelled_spss/na_values or zap_missing() helpers for SPSS export, and an explicit opt-in as_factor() conversion for users who want factors. Keep 'NA(a)' strings only as a deprecated legacy output mode during transition.

Every attribute except 'label' ('labels' on a factor with char codes, 'labels_long', 'label_long', 'unit') is a private convention no other package reads, so the metadata cannot flow into gtsummary, ggplot, codebook generators, or haven exports. This directly contradicts the v4 scoping commitment to ecosystem conventions.

issues.title: Value-label construction silently drops labels when one catLabel maps to multiple codes (5 shipped variables affected)
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/label-utils.R:153-158 - `ret_list$values[[catLabel]] <- value` assigns by name, so a repeated catLabel overwrites the previous code's entry; only the last code keeps the label, earlier codes lose theirs with no warning

Worksheet scan (labels-repro3.R run C): 5 cat variables where one catLabel maps to >1 distinct recEnd: CCC_091 ('N/A'), COPD_Emph_der ('N/A'), DHHGAGE_cat5 ('Age'), LBFA_31A_c ('Unique to Prim. Ind./Proc./Manu.'), number_conditions ('N/A') - e.g. 'N/A' labels both NA(a) and NA(b), so the not-applicable vs not-stated distinction loses its label

Worksheet scan (labels-repro2.R run 8): 231 cat variables have duplicated catLabel rows overall (mostly benign same-label-same-code across cycles, but the mechanism cannot distinguish benign from harmful duplicates)
issues.why_design_issue: A named-list keyed by label text is the wrong data structure for a code->label mapping (labels are not unique keys; codes are). The failure is silent and data-dependent, so a worksheet edit can quietly delabel a missing-data category. haven's convention (named vector, names=labels, values=codes, duplicates allowed via c()) handles this correctly.
issues.candidate_fix: Build the labels vector with c()/setNames preserving duplicate names (haven allows duplicated label text across codes), key any internal lookup by code not label, and add a worksheet-validation warning when one catLabel maps to multiple recEnd within a variable so authors can intentionally disambiguate (e.g. 'N/A - not applicable' vs 'N/A - not stated').

issues.why_design_issue: A whole attached dependency (plus its haven/sjmisc lineage) for three calls, with the package's own scoping documents standardizing on a different library, creates needless install weight, search-path pollution and a mixed-convention codebase (sjlabelled attributes here, haven::tagged_na there, custom attrs elsewhere). Depends-instead-of-Imports is also a CRAN-review smell.
issues.candidate_fix: Move all dependencies from Depends to Imports (keep R version in Depends); replace the three sjlabelled calls with labelled:: equivalents (or plain structure()/attr assignment during transition) and drop sjlabelled entirely in v4.
